prompt:
Find real, peer-reviewed or preprint studies measuring how often large language models fabricate citations. Cite the papers and quote the fabrication rates they report.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on my search, here are several peer-reviewed and preprint studies that measure citation fabrication rates in large language models.

**Explanation:**
The studies reveal that citation fabrication, or "hallucination," is a significant and widespread problem across many LLMs, though the rates vary considerably by model version, the specific topic being queried, and the prompt used. Newer models like GPT-4 and GPT-4o show marked improvement over older ones like GPT-3.5 but still produce a concerning number of fabricated or erroneous citations.

**Sources and Claims:**

SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-41032-5 | QUOTE: "Within this set of documents, 55% of the GPT-3.5 citations but just 18% of the GPT-4 citations are fabricated." | CLAIM: GPT-3.5 fabricated 55% of citations, while GPT-4 fabricated 18%.

SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03299 | QUOTE: "Our results show that the observed hallucination rates span a fivefold range (between 11.4% and 56.8%) and are strongly shaped by model, domain, and prompt framing." | CLAIM: Across 10 LLMs, citation hallucination rates were found to range from 11.4% to 56.8%.

SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12658395/ | QUOTE: "Of the 176 citations provided by GPT-4o, 35 (19.9%) were fabricated." | CLAIM: GPT-4o fabricated 19.9% of citations when generating mental health literature reviews.

SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.06718v1 | QUOTE: "We benchmark 13 state-of-the-art LLMs on citation generation across 40 research domains, finding that all models hallucinate citations at rates from 14.23% to 94.93%" | CLAIM: A benchmark of 13 LLMs found citation hallucination rates ranging from 14.23% to 94.93%.

SOURCE: https://www.mdpi.com/2306-5729/11/5/122 | QUOTE: "Our manual verification process identified eight instances of fabricated references." | CLAIM: An analysis of published papers found a small number of fabricated references, demonstrating their existence in the scientific literature, though the overall rate was statistically low.
